messages:
oncall-bot: [INCIDENT] GeoDNS anomaly detected — elevated NXDOMAIN and inconsistent A answers for app.redwood.ai from Cloudflare resolver pool in us-west-2. Rate: 8% -> 42% in the last 3m. Paging oncall SREs.

raj: seeing this on the dashboards too, latency spike for a subset of customers in us-west. Errors look correlated with specific edge ASNs.

sara: on it — pulling recent authoritative responses now. can someone run a few digs from an affected host?

eli: running dig from us-west instance:```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 app.redwood.ai A
(returns nothing / NXDOMAIN)
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 app.redwood.ai A
52.23.11.7
```

mike: same from cloudflare resolver from our probe:```
> dig @2606:4700:4700::1111 app.redwood.ai A +short
(returns NXDOMAIN)
```

raj: that aligns — Route53 answers present, Cloudflare authoritative pool seems returning NXDOMAIN for some queries. Could be propagation or an internal CF edge resolver issue.

ops-bot: automated mitigation suggestion: shift traffic away from us-west 2 for geodns fallback and increase fallback weight to route53-primary for 10m. Confirm with :thumbsup: to apply.

sara: +1, do it. we need to reduce customer impact while we investigate.

eli: applying temporary geodns weight change now:```
# geodns-cli set-weight --zone app.redwood.ai --origin route53-primary --weight 90 --duration 600
Applied: route53-primary=90, cloudflare-edge=10
```

mike: push landed. monitoring telemetry — 30s to propagate. alerting channels should show drop in NXDOMAIN if this helps.

raj: contacting Cloudflare support via ticket, adding traceroutes and dig outputs. ETA from CF on initial triage usually ~20-30m.

cloud-support: cf support here — we've opened ticket #CF-226789. Support engineer asked for full resolver logs and sample query ids; requesting a few pcap snippets from affected probes.

eli: attaching probe logs and a short pcap to the ticket. also hitting our canary via curl to confirm health endpoints:```
$ curl -sv https://app.redwood.ai/health || true
* Connected to app.redwood.ai (52.23.11.7) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: app.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

raj: good — origin is fine. this looks like inconsistent answers from the Cloudflare authoritative side or an edge resolver anomaly. also seeing a small set of customers stuck on an old NS set via certain ISP caches.

mike: quick thought — lower TTLs won't help now, but switching geodns policies to prefer route53 for affected prefixes reduces customer-facing errors. We did that. Next: consider forcing a SOA serial bump and re-announce zone from our side to encourage fresh answers.

ops-bot: action item logged: MIT-684320 — temporary geodns failover applied. owners: sara, raj. estimated mitigation complete: in progress.

sara: doing SOA refresh now — bumping serial and re-publishing zone to both providers to force revalidation.```
# terraform apply -target=module.dns.zone_publish
Apply complete. New SOA serial 2026031502
```

eli: CF ticket updated with SOA serial and timestamps. CF support confirmed they see a subset of their authoritative cache returning stale NXDOMAIN answers tied to an internal eviction bug on specific PoPs. They are routing a patch.

raj: rolling back geodns weights after CF confirms progressive fix? recommend leaving 90/10 for a bit until we see stable answers for 30m.

mike: agree. keeping 90/10 for 45m, then re-evaluate. will monitor per-customer error budgets.

cloud-support: CF estimates full propagation of the fix across their PoPs in ~18 minutes. They will provide a postmortem update when available.

ops-bot: note: customer-impact tag added. Notify CS for customers in us-west who reported errors.

sara: pinging CS with a short note and offering timeline.

raj: closing loop: once CF confirms, we'll revert weights and run a controlled canary to verify. If any residual errors, we will open a dedicated support ticket with ISPs involved.

mike: thumbs for post-incident follow-up: collect impacted customer IP ranges, time windows, and CF PoP IDs; include in postmortem.

on-message: (reacted with :rotating_light: to oncall-bot)

ops-bot: MIT-684320 status update: mitigation applied, provider engaged, monitoring. Will update when CF confirms resolution or at next 20m checkpoint.

sara: thanks team. stay on the thread for a few more checks. will update the incident doc afterwards. :white_check_mark:
